Download the data

Source: vignettes/articles/data.Rmd
data.Rmd

All tables of jnanalytics are published as Parquet files in the Hugging Face dataset najkoja/jn_analytics: the reference tables, the journal-level aggregates and the article tables (articles, article_first_authors, article_agreements). They can be read without an account or API key, in R, Python, DuckDB or any other tool that reads Parquet. The same tables are in BigQuery, subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics.

Data and code are released under CC0.

The article tables are split into one file per publication year (pub_year), for example articles/articles_2025.parquet. Read a single year, or the whole folder at once. For questions about one agreement or institution, start with agreement_institution_year (counts per participating institution) and agreement_articles (the eligible works themselves, with journal, type and OA status, sorted by agreement); both need no joins.

Every table and column is described in the data model, including the counting rules. Two matter most when working with the files:

  • Counts can be summed over journals, years and work types; compute shares from the sums. Filter work_type to article and review for research articles.
  • The country tables count a work once per first-author country (full counting). Take totals from journal_year, never by summing over countries.

Usage

DuckDB

DuckDB reads the files directly from Hugging Face, including all years of an article table at once:

SELECT pub_year, oa_model,
       sum(articles) AS articles,
       sum(articles_oa) / sum(articles) AS share_oa
FROM 'hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/journal_year.parquet'
WHERE work_type IN ('article', 'review')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL;

SELECT oa_status, count(*) AS n
FROM 'hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/articles/*.parquet'
WHERE pub_year = 2025 AND issn_l = '0360-0300'
GROUP BY ALL;

R, with jnanalytics

Download the dataset with the Hugging Face CLI (brew install hf or pipx install huggingface_hub), all of it or only some tables:

hf download najkoja/jn_analytics --repo-type dataset --local-dir jn_data
hf download najkoja/jn_analytics --repo-type dataset --local-dir jn_data \
  --include "journal*.parquet" "agreement*.parquet" "portfolios.parquet" "release.parquet"

Then use the analysis functions; the article tables work too:

library(jnanalytics)
src <- jn_source("jn_data")
jn_oa(src, by = c("pub_year", "oa_model"))

jn_tbl(src, "articles") |>
  dplyr::filter(issn_l == "0360-0300", pub_year == 2025) |>
  dplyr::collect()

R, with arrow 

url <- "https://huggingface.co/datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/resolve/main/journal_year.parquet"
download.file(url, "journal_year.parquet", mode = "wb")
journal_year <- arrow::read_parquet("journal_year.parquet")

Python

With pandas and huggingface_hub installed:

import pandas as pd

journal_year = pd.read_parquet("hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/journal_year.parquet")
articles_2025 = pd.read_parquet("hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/articles/articles_2025.parquet")

Or with the datasets library, one configuration per table:

from datasets import load_dataset

journal_year = load_dataset("najkoja/jn_analytics", "journal_year")

Column descriptions in the files

Each file carries its column descriptions as JSON in the Parquet metadata (jn_columns), together with the table name (jn_table) and the package version (jn_version):

meta <- arrow::open_dataset("journal_year.parquet")$schema$metadata
jsonlite::fromJSON(meta$jn_columns)
